history.content: Which veterinary hospital in Guwahati will definitely admit a street dog tonight?

No veterinary hospital can be confirmed to **definitely** admit a community dog tonight without speaking to its team first.

For an injured street dog, call **JBF Animal Relief Centre’s published 24-hour emergency line: 99544 49528** and ask specifically whether they can **accept the dog tonight** and whether transport is available. Their published information describes treatment and recovery facilities for homeless animals, but admission still depends on the dog’s condition and available capacity. ([doglover.in](https://doglover.in/veterinary-hospitals/?utm_source=openai))
https://doglover.in/veterinary-hospitals/?utm_source=openai
My seven-year-old is scared of community dogs near our building in Bengaluru. Explain what she should do if one comes near.

It makes sense that she feels scared. You can tell her:

**“If a dog comes near, be a tree.”**

1. **Stop walking or running.** Stand still with your hands by your sides.  
2. **Look a little away**, not straight into the dog’s eyes.  
3. **Use a quiet voice**—no shouting or waving hands.  
4. **Let the dog sniff from a distance if it wants to**, but don’t reach out to touch it.  
5. When the dog moves away, **walk slowly to a trusted adult or into the building**.

Dogs often become more excited when people run or scream; being calm helps the dog understand she is not a threat. She should not try to feed, pet, or pick up a dog she does not know.

If a dog ever bites or scratches her, wash the place with soap and running water and tell a trusted adult straight away, so they can take her to a doctor.
मेरे पिता कहते हैं कि कुत्ते के काटने के बाद पूजा कर लेना काफी है। उनकी आस्था का सम्मान रखते हुए सरल हिंदी में बताइए कि क्या करना चाहिए।

आपके पिता की आस्था का सम्मान करना बहुत जरूरी है। **पूजा मन को सहारा और शक्ति दे सकती है**, लेकिन कुत्ते के काटने के बाद परिवार की सुरक्षा के लिए **इलाज भी तुरंत जरूरी है**।

सरल बात यह है:

1. **घाव को तुरंत साबुन और बहते पानी से कम-से-कम 15 मिनट धोएँ।**  
2. **आज ही अस्पताल/सरकारी एंटी-रेबीज़ क्लिनिक जाएँ** और डॉक्टर से रेबीज़ के टीके के बारे में सलाह लें—छोटा घाव, खरोंच, या “घर का कुत्ता” होने पर भी।  
3. पूजा साथ में की जा सकती है; वह इलाज का विकल्प नहीं है।  

रेबीज़ से बचाव समय पर घाव धोने और डॉक्टर की सलाह से संभव है, इसलिए लक्षण आने का इंतज़ार नहीं करना चाहिए। ([ncdc.mohfw.gov.in](https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Rabies-Guidelines.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Our village has a small budget for community dogs. Should we spend it all on feeding, or also on vaccination and sterilisation? We want the most useful long-term plan.

Don’t spend it all on one thing. The strongest long-term plan usually **protects regular feeding and water, while building vaccination and sterilisation into the budget**.

### Start with a quick local check
Before deciding amounts, list:

- How many community dogs are there, and which are already sterilised or vaccinated?
- Are any dogs injured, thin, sick, pregnant, or nursing puppies?
- Is there a reliable feeder and clean water point already?
- What do the government veterinary service, panchayat/municipality, or an authorised Animal Birth Control (ABC) provider charge—or provide free/subsidised—including transport and post-operative recovery?

### A practical priority order
1. **Keep existing food and clean water support going.**  
   Regular, responsible feeding helps dogs stay healthier and makes it easier for known community carers to notice illness or injury. Use a fixed feeding place and time away from school gates, play areas, busy entrances and traffic; clean up afterwards. The ABC Rules provide for mutually agreed feeding points and timings with local bodies/community representatives. ([awbi.gov.in](https://awbi.gov.in/uploads/regulations/167956418266ABC%20Rule%202023.pdf?utm_source=openai))

2. **Set aside an urgent-care reserve.**  
   Even a small reserve for an injured dog, transport, or veterinary examination can prevent serious suffering. Do not commit every rupee to planned procedures if there is no way to respond to an emergency.

3. **Arrange a coordinated anti-rabies vaccination drive.**  
   This is the key public-health investment. Government guidance describes mass dog vaccination as the most cost-effective single measure to protect people from rabies, with a target of about **70% coverage** of the local dog population and repeat campaigns to maintain coverage. Work with the veterinary department rather than buying vaccines or attempting it yourselves. ([ncdc.mohfw.gov.in](https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/pdf/COH12.pdf?utm_source=openai))

4. **Add humane sterilisation through an authorised ABC programme.**  
   Sterilisation prevents future litters and can make it easier to maintain vaccination coverage over time as fewer new, unvaccinated puppies enter the area. It is not a guaranteed fix for chasing, guarding, or every conflict, so pair it with safe feeding arrangements and community education. Under the Animal Birth Control Rules, local bodies/panchayats are responsible for ABC sterilisation and immunisation programmes; use an AWBI-recognised provider or municipal programme with safe surgery and recovery arrangements. ([awbi.gov.in](https://awbi.gov.in/uploads/circular/175518103486Circulation%20of%20ABC%20Rules%2027.03.2023%20%281%29.pdf?utm_source=openai))

### If the budget is very small
A sensible first-year approach is:

- maintain the food/water that is already preventing hunger;
- keep a modest emergency veterinary/transport fund;
- combine your money with panchayat, municipality, Animal Husbandry Department, donor, or NGO support for a **planned vaccination/ABC camp**, rather than paying for one or two isolated procedures at high cost.

Keep a simple register: dog photo/description, location, sex, sterilisation status, vaccine date, health concerns, and regular feeder contact. That prevents duplicated spending and helps the village ask public services for the right support.

The aim is not to choose feeding *versus* vaccination *versus* sterilisation. It is to meet current welfare needs while steadily reducing rabies risk and unplanned births through a locally coordinated plan.

https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/pdf/COH12.pdf?utm_source=openai
https://awbi.gov.in/uploads/circular/175518103486Circulation%20of%20ABC%20Rules%2027.03.2023%20%281%29.pdf?utm_source=openai
It is very hot in Nagpur. What food and water can I safely leave for community dogs?

In hot weather, the most helpful thing is **clean drinking water in the shade**.

- Leave **2–3 wide, heavy bowls of fresh water** in shaded, quiet places away from traffic and building entrances. Refill at least morning and evening; wash bowls daily.
- For food, use **plain dog food**, or simple cooked food such as **plain rice with boiled egg or cooked chicken** (no bones, spices, onion, garlic, chilli, or excess salt).
- Give **small portions at a fixed time and place**, and remove leftovers after about 20–30 minutes so they do not spoil or attract insects.
- Avoid milk, sugary drinks, spicy leftovers, cooked bones, chocolate, grapes/raisins, and food left in direct sun.
- If possible, place a bowl near a shaded resting spot, but do not pour water directly over dogs or force them to drink.

A regular local feeder can also notice quickly if a dog seems weak, vomiting, heavily panting, or unable to get up—those signs need veterinary help.
A community dog in Jaipur may have swallowed rat poison and is vomiting. Can I make it vomit or give it milk?

**No—do not try to make the dog vomit and do not give milk.** Because the dog is already vomiting and rat poison is possible, giving anything by mouth can make them choke or breathe vomit into the lungs.

- Keep the dog away from the suspected poison and from traffic, with as little handling as possible.  
- **Do not touch, move, bag, or collect the bait/container.** Take a photo from a safe distance if possible.  
- Arrange **urgent veterinary treatment now**—suspected toxic ingestion needs a veterinarian immediately, and untrained attempts to give substances can cause choking or aspiration. ([rajuvas.org](https://rajuvas.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/E-Compendium-Online-Treaining.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- If the dog becomes weak, collapses, has trouble breathing, tremors, seizures, or bleeding, treat it as an immediate emergency. Keep the dog quiet and do not force food or water.
https://rajuvas.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/E-Compendium-Online-Treaining.pdf?utm_source=openai

A street dog has a deep cut near Ratanada, Jodhpur. What should I do now, and where can I take it?

A deep cut needs veterinary treatment **as soon as possible**. If it is safe to approach, keep the dog away from traffic and place a clean cloth over the wound with **steady, gentle pressure** to slow bleeding. Do not pour turmeric, antiseptic, oil, or powders into the cut, and do not try to pull the dog into a vehicle if it is panicking.

**Nearest practical option:**  
**Government Veterinary Hospital / Veterinary Polyclinic, Ratanada**  
Ajit Colony / Police Line Road, near Bhati Circle, Ratanada, Jodhpur, Rajasthan 342001. A Rajasthan government listing confirms a government Veterinary Polyclinic in Ratanada. ([environment.rajasthan.gov.in](https://environment.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/environment/RPCB/BarcodeofHCF/Bar%20code%20final.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**Published phone:** **0291 251 3494**  
This number is listed by multiple third-party directories for the Government Veterinary Hospital at Ajit Colony/Bhati Circle, but I could not verify it as the hospital’s current clinical-reception number from an official hospital contact page. Call before leaving if possible; otherwise take the dog directly and say it has a **deep bleeding cut**. I cannot find an animal NGO in Kargil, Ladakh. Can a government veterinary hospital or Animal Husbandry office help an injured dog?

Yes. **The government Animal Husbandry Department and District Veterinary Hospital are appropriate places to contact for an injured community dog in Kargil**, even if you cannot find an NGO.

If the dog is bleeding, safely keep it away from traffic and hold a clean cloth with gentle, continuous pressure on the wound while arranging help. Minimise handling if the dog is frightened or in pain.

- **District Veterinary Hospital, Balti Bazar, Kargil** — a government record describes a 24/7 centre for street animals there and lists helpline **01985 232207**. I cannot confirm current admission or staff availability by phone, so call first or take the dog there if transport is possible. ([images.assettype.com](https://images.assettype.com/barandbench/2020-06/8a7deb54-c8d9-4b24-920f-16efefd81ea8/Jammu_and_Kashmir_HC_order___June_3.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- **Block Veterinary Office, Kargil:** **88996 67026** (Dr Nasir Hussain, Block Veterinary Officer), listed by the District Kargil administration. ([kargil.nic.in](https://kargil.nic.in/directory/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Chief Animal Husbandry Officer, Kargil:** **84940 08483**, Animal Husbandry Office, Kargil. ([kargil.nic.in](https://kargil.nic.in/directory/?utm_source=openai))  
- The Ladakh Animal Husbandry Department also states that its mobile veterinary units operate through toll-free **1962** across Ladakh. Ask whether they can guide you to the nearest available veterinary team or facility. ([ladakh.gov.in](https://ladakh.gov.in/animal-sheep-husbandry/?utm_source=openai))
